classification.difficultyReason: Direct application of the taught output absolute-value rule to a linear function, followed by recognising its vertex among four supplied graphs.

content.prompt: The graph of $f(x)=x+2$ is shown as a dotted line. Which graph represents $y=|x+2|$?

spec.description: Option A: solid upward V with vertex (0,2), superimposed on the dashed source line through (-2,0) and (0,2). Arrowed Cartesian axes, integer ticks from -3 to 3 excluding zero, no grid and no curve endpoint markers. The source origin O is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Solid option: y=|x|+2. Dashed source graph: y=x+2, matching the corrected f(x)=x+2.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option letter are permanent student-visible givens; no answer selection is shown.

spec.description: Option B: solid upward V with vertex (-2,0), passing through (0,2). The dashed source line has a visible lower-left continuation and overlaps the solid right branch. Arrowed Cartesian axes, integer ticks from -3 to 3 excluding zero, no grid and no curve endpoint markers. The source origin O is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Solid option: y=|x+2|, matching the corrected target. Dashed source graph: y=x+2, matching the corrected f(x)=x+2.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option letter are permanent student-visible givens; the supplied source answer B is excluded from the question diagram.

spec.description: Option C: solid upward V with vertex (0,-2) and x-intercepts -2 and 2, superimposed on the dashed source line through (-2,0) and (0,2). Arrowed Cartesian axes, integer ticks from -3 to 3 excluding zero, no grid and no curve endpoint markers. The source origin O is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Solid option: y=|x|-2. Dashed source graph: y=x+2, matching the corrected f(x)=x+2.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option letter are permanent student-visible givens; no answer selection is shown.

spec.description: Option D: solid upward V with vertex (2,0), passing through (0,2), superimposed on the dashed source line through (-2,0) and (0,2). Arrowed Cartesian axes, integer ticks from -3 to 3 excluding zero, no grid and no curve endpoint markers. The source origin O is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Solid option: y=|x-2|, a distractor for the corrected target y=|x+2|. Dashed source graph: y=x+2, matching the corrected f(x)=x+2.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option letter are permanent student-visible givens; no answer selection is shown.

answer.worked:
Keep the graph of $f(x)=x+2$ on and above the $x$-axis unchanged and reflect the portion below it across the $x$-axis. The resulting V has vertex $(-2,0)$ and passes through $(0,2)$.

Correct answer: B.
